$doc: The UI's protocol with the core: its commands, by number (@xpute/kit/abi/cmd.ts:
`major << 8 | minor`, past xpute's majors 0x00 to 0x0F), each with the packet
it carries — an XTP branch whose children are its fields, in order. A command with no
fields carries no packet. The JavaScript around the core is two
things to it, its runtime, which holds the turns and carries its imports to what
answers them (ts/client/src/service/sys/), and its UI, which sends what the user
does and what the place's sensors, visibility and frames tell it
(ts/client/src/service/core/). A command's major is the module it is for.
`export` is what the UI sends the core and `import` what the core posts to it, `call`
one its sender waits on. Each is written and read by what this file generates, on
both sides, so no field is found by its position anywhere else.
A field is a number of a width, a `bool`, a `str`, a member of an enum
below or of one another spec declares (`extern`), or a record below. An
`optional` one may be absent, its kind kept; a `list` is a branch of them,
or a packed array where the item is a number. A record crosses as a branch
of its own fields, and is how a block past a slot is laid out. An enum's
`unknown` is the member a number it does not give out reads as; an enum
without one refuses the packet. The generator refuses a number given twice.
name: ui

export.name: SENSOR_POS
$doc: A GPS fix; a field is absent where the browser gave none.

export.name: SENSOR_ORIENT
$doc: An orientation event; a field is absent where the browser gave none.

export.name: SENSOR_ERR
$doc: A watch that ended in failure and was stopped, refused from the start (PermissionDenied)
or cut off; the compass's, where the platform says so (SYS_BOOT's
orient_silence_is_loss).

pkt.name: code
$doc: Geolocation's; orientation gives none.

export.name: TURN_GRANT
$doc: What the runtime's frame pacing grants the turn it rings next, sent before its
SYS_TURN (@xpute/runtime), which carries the clock: the frame's budget and whether
it follows an input.

pkt.name: refresh_ms
$doc: The display's refresh, as the runtime measures it from the animation frames it is handed,
and the interval it paces turns at, a whole number of refreshes (the pacing the client
boots it with, @xpute/runtime sched/frame_pacing.ts `FrameGrant`): the frame's budget.

export.name: SOURCE_DECLARE
$doc: What the tile source declares of itself, once the client has it: the tile root's
`source`, the published one out of the bucket or the dev tile server's, read by the
client (ts/client/src/service/sys/fs/source.ts) and handed over as numbers and names.
Until it comes nothing is observed: the floor is held at the zoom it names, and no
tile is asked for that no shard it serves is over or under (pxl-core sys/io/source.rs).

pkt.name: min_zoom
$doc: The coarsest zoom the source supplies whole.

pkt.name: format
$doc: Each kind's format, one a kind, indexed by its bake's number
(pxl-spec bake/publication.spec.rs).

pkt.name: shard
$doc: The shards it serves, by name. Their order means nothing: no two at a zoom
are over one node, and the finer wins.

export.name: SENSOR_PERMISSION
$doc: A permission as the UI's prompt or the browser's change reported it.

export.name: SENSOR_PLATFORM
$doc: What the place's sensors are: whether it has a position and a heading, whether the
heading asks a permission, and how it says it is lost. Sent once the core is attached.

pkt.name: orient_permission
$doc: iOS 13+'s gate: requestPermission exists and must run inside a gesture.

pkt.name: orient_silence_is_loss
$doc: A browser's compass talks while the device is still and cannot say it stopped, so
silence is the only sign of loss; a device's speaks only when the heading turns and
reports a failure itself (SENSOR_ERR).

export.name: SETTING_DEV
$doc: Whether this is a development build, which offers the settings schema.json marks `dev`.
Sent once the core is attached.

export.name: INPUT_POINTER
$doc: A pointer event on the world's canvas, in CSS pixels from the top left of its layout box
(transforms aside), as the world surface's size is (GPU_SURFACE_RESIZE).

export.name: EDIT_TOOL
$doc: The tool and what it takes, the UI's to choose and keep: the core is told, and answers EINVAL for an item the catalog does not give out. It picks again under a hovering pointer.

pkt.name: val
$doc: The item to place, its id (id.json); read only for that tool.

pkt.name: scale_steps
$doc: A cube's scale, as a decor's `scale_steps`: 0 a unit, each step down its half, to 1 - OBJECT_SCALES (pxl-spec bake/object.spec.rs). Read only for an item, and only a cube's is chosen.

export.name: EDIT_MARKER_TEXT
$doc: The draft's text (Snapshot.draft), which the marker is drawn with and committed with. Text past MARKER_TEXT_CHARS (spec/spec/asset/marker.json) is refused whole, never cut: EMSGSIZE, which the UI shows as what does not fit.

export.name: EDIT_MARKER_COMMIT
$doc: The marker's draft committed with its text, where its place is still free or still a marker, and closed.

export.name: INPUT_MOVE
$doc: The screen direction the held movement keys point, sent when it changes: each axis -1, 0 or 1, x to the right and y down.

export.name: SCENE_DRAW
$doc: What a surface the UI opened draws, until its GPU_SURFACE_CLOSE. The world, with the
sensors watched while it shows; or the companion's character of a group alone, as the picker shows it, a second one
on the same surface replacing the first. EBADF where the surface is not open, EBUSY where it already draws the
other content, EINVAL where the character's fields are not all given for a character or any is given for the
world.

pkt.name: bg
$doc: What the character is drawn over, 0xRRGGBB, sRGB.

export.name: SETTING_SET
$doc: A setting set from the sheet or the character picker; refused until the core has read the
kept settings, which would be read over it.

pkt.name: val
$doc: A toggle's 0 or 1, a choice's option by its index, or a number.

export.name: SCENE_CHAT
$doc: A line the player said, shown over the character.

export.name: CAMERA_TRACKING
$doc: The tracking button's press, as the button showed it.

export.name: CAMERA_NORTH_UP
$doc: The compass was pressed: north comes up.

export.name: SENSOR_LOCATE
$doc: The search panel's location card's press: the location asked for. The compass is
asked for where it is used, entering follow mode (TRACKING), and never alone: nothing
reads it without the location.

export.name: CAMERA_GOTO
$doc: A search result: the pivot moved there, and the view asked with it at once, as the
controls ask it where the camera stands; a view field absent keeps what the view has.

pkt.name: dist
$doc: The zoom, the eye's distance from the pivot, clamped to the zoom's range; absent, a view far out comes in.

pkt.name: azimuth
$doc: The heading about Z in radians, wrapped.

pkt.name: polar
$doc: The angle down from vertical in radians, clamped.

export.name: INPUT_XR_POSE
$doc: A tracked pose: where a tracker has the camera, and its turn as a unit quaternion
(x, y, z, w) from the camera's axes to the tracker's, in the world's units. The
first of a run is taken to be where the camera already is, so nothing moves as
it begins; the camera follows the tracker from there until POSE_END. Nothing in the
client sends it: it is the way in for an immersive mode's head pose (a Quest's, a
Vision Pro's) to drive the camera, from the device app.

export.name: INPUT_XR_POSE_END
$doc: The tracker let the camera go: back to the controller it had.

export.name: PERF_START
$doc: Starts a fresh recording window.

export.name: PERF_STOP
$doc: Freezes the window, so what is exported holds still.

export.name: PERF_STATS
$doc: The profiler's statistics and what it holds now, where they lie: the reply is the address of STAT_SLOT's words (perf.json), the statistics
over the last `window_ms`, the whole recording where it is absent, good until the next turn. A
number past the door is finite, so no window is infinite.

export.name: PERF_RINGS
$doc: The rings where they lie, nothing reduced: the reply is the address of RING_SLOT's words (perf.json), good until the next turn.

import.name: UI_SNAPSHOT
$doc: The UI's snapshot, when it changed: a Snapshot packet far past a ring frame, so a
block the core holds, valid until the next snapshot.

import.name: UI_VIEW
$doc: The view's azimuth and scale, when either moved: a frame of its own, so a rotation or a
zoom, which moves them every frame, leaves the snapshot as it was.

pkt.name: m_per_px
$doc: The meters a logical pixel spans at the pivot, at the camera's distance; 0 where the camera stands there. The scale bar is the UI's to make of it; which division names show, the core's (`DivisionPart.shown`).

import.name: TURN_PACE
$doc: The least interval the core asks between its turns: its load's word on the rate, which
the next TURN_GRANT's `paced_ms` answers, a whole number of refreshes (the pacing the
client boots the runtime with, @xpute/runtime sched/frame_pacing.ts `pace`). A core on
its own thread sets it there and posts nothing (xpute-core sched/frame.rs).

pkt.name: interval_ms
$doc: 0 asks none, and turns go at the display's own rate.

extern.name: BakeKind
$doc: By its index in BAKE_KINDS (publication.spec.ts).

extern.name: SettingKey
$doc: A setting by its `number` in schema.json's SETTING.

extern.name: CharacterGroup
$doc: character.json's group, by its number.

entries.name: Cancel
$doc: The pointer's gesture ends with no tap: the platform took it, or the UI spent it on something of its own.

enums.name: PointerType
$doc: What the pointer is, as the browser's `pointerType` says.

enums.name: Tool
$doc: What the pointer holds: itself, the eraser, or an item to place, which its id says the kind of.

entries.name: Recenter
$doc: The camera goes back to the device's place.

entries.name: Follow
$doc: Follow mode on, where the compass is listened to.

entries.name: Unfollow
$doc: Follow mode off, north up again.

enums.name: GeolocationErrorCode
$doc: The browser's PositionError codes.

entries.name: Asking
$doc: The UI's prompt is up.

entries.name: Failed
$doc: The prompt itself threw.

enums.name: GroundStatus
$doc: Whether the screen shows the world: Success once a frame that drew ground went
to it, or one went over a view whose tiles all answered with nothing to draw;
Loading until then, on a first load, after a jump or a lost device; Idle before
there is a view.

enums.name: SensorStatus
$doc: Where a sensor's reading is: none asked for, asked for, arriving, failed, or none to be had, the device having no such sensor.

enums.name: Message
$doc: A message the core raises and the UI shows.
The core decides which message a state calls for and carries the number.
It never carries the words: a string that exists to be read has no reason
to sit in the core's memory, and the UI has the locale files already
(ts/client/src/ui/shared/locale) — the same split `strerror` is on the other side of.
The number is the name here, and a band is what a message is about.

entries.section: 0x02 where the device says it is
0x03 which way the device is facing
0x04 why the server does not answer the world's reads

entries.name: WorldReadFailing
$doc: Reads reach the server and fail; they are tried again.

entries.name: WorldUnavailable
$doc: Reads failed past every retry; the world is not coming.

records.name: Snapshot
$doc: What the page's UI shows of the core (ui.rs): written after a turn that changed it, and replaced whole.

fields.name: draft
$doc: A marker's draft, its text so far, absent where none is open: opened by the marker tool's tap, with the marker's own text where one stands there, empty where it is new, and closed by EDIT_MARKER_COMMIT or EDIT_MARKER_CANCEL.

fields.name: zooming
$doc: A zoom is in hand: two fingers are down, or a wheel's zoom is still arriving. The scale is shown while it is.

fields.name: over_marker
$doc: The pointer is over a scene marker a tap would act on with the tool held: a place to go to, or a pin to erase or draft.

fields.name: settings
$doc: Every setting's value by its SettingKey, as SETTING_SET carries one; none until the core
has read its storage file, a few turns from boot.

fields.name: division
$doc: The division the pivot is in and every one above it, broad to narrow; empty
where the pivot is in none or the tile it is read out of has not arrived.

fields.name: character_surfaces
$doc: The surfaces a character is drawn on: its model and skin have arrived. The UI shows one loading until its surface is here.

fields.name: refused_files
$doc: The files the core refused, not of their format, not decoding, or too large for any
heap: a storage file (file.json's `storage`) or a placed objects' file (`object`). The
core read none of it and writes nothing over it until FS_CHANGED says it is
empty.

fields.name: stall
$doc: Why the server does not answer the world's reads now: failing since the last answered, or given up. Absent while it answers. The network and the GPU are the runtime's to say.

fields.name: renderer_progress
$doc: How much of what the renderer makes before its first frame is made, 0 to 1 (pxl-render gpu/pipeline.rs `PipelineCache::share`): the pipelines made of those asked for, in whatever order they finish, 0 before any is asked; 1 once it draws, 0 again while a lost device's next renderer is made. The loading bar is the UI's to draw of it.

fields.name: area_progress
$doc: How much of the view's ground shows, 0 to 1: of the tiles asked for, those with an answer or drawn coarser. 0 where none is asked yet, 1 once the area is shown; it goes back as more is asked for.

fields.name: lon_lat
$doc: The pivot in degrees: what the search measures distance from.

fields.name: outside
$doc: The pivot is past the service area: the source serves no shard over it (pxl-core sys/io/source.rs).

fields.name: err
$doc: Present exactly when status is Error: the failure the core chose.

fields.name: err
$doc: Present exactly when status is Error: the failure the core chose.

records.name: DivisionPart
$doc: One division of the name, in its own name.

fields.name: subtype
$doc: Overture's subtype, broadest first (spec/spec/division.json).

fields.name: shown
$doc: The view is in far enough for its name to show: as far as Overture's own tiles
show it from (pxl-spec bake/tile/division.rs `Division::shown_from`).

fields.name: area
$doc: Held by an area the point is in; one without is the nearest found by its point.

fields.name: root
$doc: file.json's `root`.

fields.name: path
$doc: Its path below the root, as the core opened it.
